editorial:
Imagine growing up in a house where you only have one person you can actually trust. That is exactly the situation Lela and Vid find themselves in. They are siblings who have spent their whole lives sticking together to survive their parents' toxic behavior. The movie does a great job of making you feel the warmth between the siblings while showing how cold their home life really is. It sets up a heavy, emotional mood that builds up toward the big party on New Years Eve, making you really root for them to find a way out together.

The acting is the best part here because the chemistry between the lead actors feels totally real. While the movie starts a bit slow, the tension spikes in the final act and keeps you glued to your seat. If you like stories about family secrets and emotional breakouts, you will love this. For the best experience, you should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the small details in the set design. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a smart move for a movie this polished.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart during the countdown to the year 2000. Lela discovers that Vid has been lying about a way for them to escape their parents. In a heated argument, a secret about their father comes out that turns the siblings against each other. Instead of leaving together, they end up saying things they can never take back. The movie ends with them walking away in opposite directions, showing their bond is permanently broken.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves deep family dramas and emotional stories.
